proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the defining property of the floor function, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. In particular, floor(x) itself is an integer satisfying floor(x) <= x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: The floor of a real number is, by definition, an integer no larger than that number. Therefore floor(x) <= x for all real x.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly shows that for an arbitrary real x, floor(x) is an integer and satisfies floor(x) <= x, which is exactly the lemma statement. No semantic drift or dependency issue is present.
